story.title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears
story.description: Lost in the forest, a girl wanders into the empty home of a family of bears and tries out everything she finds.
story.author: Traditional English folklore

chapters.name: Lost in the Woods
chapters.summary: Goldilocks is told where not to go, goes there, and finds a house whose owners have never had a reason to lock anything.

chapters.name: Three of Everything
chapters.summary: Every object in the house belongs to exactly one of the bears. Goldilocks works through all three sizes of each, and breaks the smallest of them.

chapters.name: The Bears Come Home
chapters.summary: The bears find the evidence in the order Goldilocks left it, room by room, until the last thing they find is her.

scenes.name: Told not to wander
scenes.summary: Her mother sends Goldilocks on an errand and names the one path she is to keep to. The warning is specific, which is how the reader knows it will be ignored.

scenes.name: The path that was wrong
scenes.summary: A woodcutter gives her directions that would have been right yesterday. By the time the trees close in behind her, Goldilocks can no longer say which way she came.

scenes.name: A house among the trees
scenes.summary: A small house stands in a clearing with its door pushed to and nobody in sight. There is smoke in the chimney and something cooling on the table, which means whoever lives here has only just stepped out.

scenes.name: Nobody answers
scenes.summary: Goldilocks knocks twice, waits, and lets herself in. Nothing in the house resists her, and she takes the absence of a lock for the absence of an owner.

scenes.name: Three bowls of porridge
scenes.summary: Three bowls sit cooling on the kitchen table in three sizes. The largest is too hot and the middle one too cold; the smallest is exactly right, so she finishes it.

scenes.name: Three chairs
scenes.summary: Three chairs stand by the fire. The big one is too hard and the middle one too soft, and Goldilocks keeps testing rather than stopping at the first that would have done.

scenes.name: The smallest chair breaks
scenes.summary: The third chair fits her exactly and gives way under her. It is the first thing she cannot put back the way she found it, and she leaves the pieces where they fall.

scenes.name: Three beds
scenes.summary: Upstairs there are three beds, and the same test runs a third time. She falls asleep in the smallest of them, in a stranger's house, with the door still unlatched behind her.

scenes.name: Someone has been at my porridge
scenes.summary: The three bears come home to a kitchen that has been used. Two bowls have been stirred and set down again; the third has been emptied, and Baby Bear is the one who says so.

scenes.name: Someone has been sitting in my chair
scenes.summary: Two chairs have been moved. The third is in pieces on the floor, and the discovery stops being an annoyance and becomes a loss the moment its owner sees it.

scenes.name: Someone is sleeping in my bed
scenes.summary: Two beds are rumpled. In the third there is a girl, still asleep, and the three bears stand looking at her with no idea at all what they are supposed to do next.

scenes.name: Out through the window
scenes.summary: Goldilocks wakes to three bears at the foot of the bed and is out of the window before anyone speaks. Nobody chases her; the bears are as frightened as she is, and they are the ones left with the mess.

characters.name: Goldilocks
characters.description: A curious girl who loses her way on an errand and treats an empty house as an invitation. She is not malicious; she simply never once asks whether she is allowed.
characters.personality: Curious and impulsive, quick to help herself to whatever catches her eye.
characters.motivation: Just wants to rest and eat after getting lost - and can't resist trying everything in an empty house.
characters.qualities: Adventurous and unbothered by walking into a stranger's home uninvited.
characters.weaknesses: Never stops to consider that the house belongs to someone until it's far too late.
characters.biography: A girl who wanders off the path home through the forest and stumbles on the Three Bears' empty house.
characters.plannedTimeline: Flees out the window when the bears return, and is never seen in the forest again.

characters.name: Papa Bear
characters.description: The largest of the three bears, owner of the big bowl, the hard chair and the long bed. He speaks first at every discovery, and loudest.
characters.personality: Gruff but even-tempered, the first to notice something is wrong in the house.
characters.motivation: Wants only to come home to a peaceful meal after a walk in the woods.
characters.qualities: Observant - the first to notice his porridge and chair have been disturbed.
characters.weaknesses: His big, booming voice tends to announce trouble before anyone can act on it.
characters.biography: The father of the bear family, whose oversized bowl, chair, and bed set the pattern Goldilocks tries all three of.
characters.plannedTimeline: Returns home to find every one of his belongings disturbed, and joins in discovering the sleeping intruder.

characters.name: Mama Bear
characters.description: The middle bear, owner of the middle bowl, the soft chair and the middle bed. She notices the state of a room before she notices what is missing from it.
characters.personality: Practical and quick to keep the household in order.
characters.motivation: Wants the family's home and belongings kept just the way they should be.
characters.qualities: Even-keeled - the calmest of the three when the mess is discovered.
characters.weaknesses: Her medium-sized things are always the ones passed over as "not quite right" by Goldilocks.
characters.biography: The mother of the bear family, whose porridge, chair, and bed are each tried and rejected in turn.
characters.plannedTimeline: Discovers her own belongings disturbed just before Baby Bear finds his ruined entirely.

characters.name: Baby Bear
characters.description: The smallest of the three bears, and the only one who actually loses anything: his porridge, his chair, and finally the sight of a stranger in his bed.
characters.personality: High-pitched and easily upset - the one who suffers the most from Goldilocks's visit.
characters.motivation: Just wants his breakfast, his chair, and his bed left exactly as he left them.
characters.qualities: The most sympathetic of the three - everything sized just for him is the one thing Goldilocks likes best, and ruins.
characters.weaknesses: Too small to stop anything - his soup is eaten, his chair is broken, and his bed is slept in before he ever gets a say.
characters.biography: The youngest of the bear family, whose porridge, chair, and bed turn out to be exactly Goldilocks's size.
characters.plannedTimeline: Finds his chair broken and Goldilocks asleep in his own bed, the moment that finally wakes her and sends her fleeing.

characters.name: The Woodcutter
characters.description: A woodcutter working the far side of the forest, who gives Goldilocks directions in good faith and never learns what they cost her.

characters.name: Goldilocks's Mother
characters.description: The one person in the story who states a rule out loud, right at the beginning, and is not present for a single moment of what follows.

locations.name: The Forest
locations.description: Dense woods with one path through them and a great many ways off it. Everyone who lives here knows the way; Goldilocks is the only person in the story who does not.
locations.climate: Thick with trees and easy to get lost in, with no clear paths to follow.

locations.name: The Three Bears' House
locations.description: A small house in a clearing, furnished throughout in three sizes. The door has no lock, because in all the years the bears have lived here nobody has ever come to it.
locations.climate: Warm and homely, freshly emptied while the porridge cools from breakfast.
locations.culture: A small, orderly bear family household where everything - bowls, chairs, beds - comes in a big, medium, and small size.

locations.name: The Kitchen
locations.description: Where the porridge is made and set out to cool in three bowls, during the half-hour the bears spend walking so that it will be cool enough to eat.

locations.name: The Sitting Room
locations.description: The room by the fire with the three chairs - the only room in the house where something ends up broken.

locations.name: The Upstairs Bedroom
locations.description: The room under the roof with three beds side by side, where the smallest is short enough for a child and long enough for Goldilocks.

worldRules.title: Curiosity Without Permission
worldRules.description: Walking in uninvited and trying what is not yours is never punished in this story, and never excused either. Goldilocks loses nothing at all; the bears are left with an empty bowl and a broken chair, and that asymmetry is the whole of the lesson.

worldRules.title: Three of Everything
worldRules.description: The house is furnished in three sizes and every object in it belongs to exactly one bear. Nothing here is communal or anonymous, which is why each discovery has a specific owner to be wronged by it.

worldRules.title: The House Was Never Locked
worldRules.description: Nobody in the forest locks a door, because nobody in the forest has ever needed to. What Goldilocks does is only possible because the bears live somewhere that has never required the precaution, and that is why their reaction is fright rather than anger.

notes.title: Continuity: the half-hour of porridge
notes.body: The bears are only out walking because the porridge is too hot. The whole story fits inside the time it takes to cool, and no scene should imply they were gone longer than that.

notes.title: Visual motif: three, then one
notes.body: Every discovery is staged the same way - big, middle, small - and lands on the smallest. Keep the rhythm identical across porridge, chairs and beds so that the last one carries the weight.

notes.title: Revision goal: nobody is a villain
notes.body: Goldilocks is not a thief and the bears are not monsters. Every scene should be readable as an accident between people who never expected to meet.

items.name: Baby Bear's Bowl of Porridge
items.description: The smallest of the three bowls left cooling on the table, made to a size nobody else in the house would want. It is the only one that is exactly right, and the only one that ends up empty.

items.name: Baby Bear's Chair
items.description: The smallest of the three chairs by the fire, built for someone the size of its owner. It is the one thing in the house Goldilocks cannot put back as she found it.

items.name: Baby Bear's Bed
items.description: The smallest of the three beds under the roof, short enough for its owner and, as it turns out, exactly long enough for a lost girl.
